title: Desk Training Questions: Early-Booking Relief on the Advance for a Respite or Trial Stay
content:
**Rule.** For the advance on a booked stay under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement, the early-booking relief is five percent (5 percent) when the stay was booked twenty-one or more days (21 or more) before its planned arrival date, two percent (2 percent) when it was booked fourteen to twenty days (14 to 20) before, and nothing otherwise.

## Questions answered

**How are the days counted?** As the planned arrival date less the booking date recorded on the stay, in calendar days.

**What does the relief reduce?** The advance-nights charge — the advance nights times the nightly rate locked at booking — as it stands, and nothing else in the advance. The charge is multiplied by 95 percent at 5 percent and by 98 percent at 2 percent.

**A stay booked on 1 March for arrival on 22 March?** 21 days: 5 percent.

**Booked on 2 March for the same arrival?** 20 days: 2 percent.

**Booked on 8 March?** 14 days: 2 percent.

**Booked on 9 March?** 13 days: nothing.

## Summary

| Days from booking to planned arrival | Early-booking relief |
|---|---|
| 21 or more | 5 percent |
| 14 to 20 | 2 percent |
| 13 or fewer | Nothing |

## Hypothetical illustration

An advance-nights charge of 1,673.00 on a stay booked 30 days ahead is 1,673.00 times 95 percent, that is 1,589.35.
